newsitem.title: DENMARK: Becalmed Danish shares edge up, little change seen.
newsitem.headline: Becalmed Danish shares edge up, little change seen.

text.p: Danish share prices closed slightly higher in a market becalmed by London's early May holiday closure, with dealers seeing no immediate swing back into any activity of note in a market set to follow U.S. trends.
"Danish investors are inactive, London has been closed so the market has been moribund. I cannot see any change up front, we will echo Wall Street tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.78 point up at 157.63, while the KFX June future rose 1.60 point to 158.30 with 190 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
The market failed to react much to the government's new green economic package, although SAS fell 1.50 crowns to close at 70 in low turnover, hit by proposed passenger air travel tax increases.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.201 billion crowns.
